name: Offensive Threat Modeling
description: Before committing to a social engineering or physical bypass approach, a red team operator performs threat modeling from the attacker's perspective — enumerating all viable access vectors, scoring each by probability of success and risk of detection, and selecting the optimal attack path. This involves mapping the target's security controls identified during recon against the team's available techniques, asking which approach (pure SE, pure physical, wireless-enabled SE, combined) gives the highest success probability with the lowest signature. Attack trees are the primary tool: each root node is an objective, branches are techniques, and leaves are specific actions. Offensive threat modeling is what separates a rehearsed, high-confidence engagement from improvised guesswork.

blue.det: No direct detection — this is pre-engagement planning; OSINT activity may be detectable via web logs or LinkedIn monitoring.
blue.cm: Monitor for unusual employee profile lookups on LinkedIn; Google dork alerts for your domain; Shodan monitoring for exposed assets; security awareness about OSINT exposure.
